$comment: OPTIONAL fifth game doc. Create it only if the game needs a real bitmap file (a texture, a sprite, a title illustration) -- most puzzle/board games need none, and then this file does not exist. It is a machine-readable run-list: hand it, plus docs/templates/game-docs/art-assets.prompt.md, to an image-generating AI agent and it writes every file. RULE FOR `prompt`: each one must be fully self-contained -- state the subject, the style, the palette with hex codes, the framing, the aspect ratio, the background, and the 'no text' constraint, all inside the prompt string -- so a human can copy any single `prompt` value into any image model and run it with no other context. Do not rely on the sibling fields to carry an instruction; they (`aspect`, `resize`, `transparency`, `background`, `chromaKey`) only restate facts in machine form and drive post-processing. Never paraphrase a `prompt`. Human context goes in the sibling art-assets.md.
globalConstraints: No text, letters, numbers, logos or watermarks anywhere in any image (a word baked into a bitmap is a string the i18n layer cannot translate -- building-a-game.md rule 11). Every prompt already says this; it is repeated here as the review checklist.
<house style, e.g. flat vector / sticker style, clean edges, even flat lighting, no photorealism>
Keep each file small -- it is precached by the service worker and downloaded before the game plays offline.
public/icon.svg and the catalog `cover` are NOT in this list -- they stay hand-authored vector (they must read at 42px).

assets.role: <one line: where this is drawn and how>
assets.background: opaque, the image fills the frame
assets.prompt: <one paragraph, self-contained. Subject in full, then: '<style> illustration style, no photorealism', the palette with hex codes, the framing ('centered, filling most of a square 1:1 frame' or 'fills the entire frame, tiles seamlessly'), even flat lighting. End with: 'Do not include any text, letters, numbers, logos or watermarks.'>
assets.acceptCheck: <what a human confirms by eye before committing>

assets.background: flat magenta #FF00FF, no gradient, no shadow
assets.chromaKey: src/assets.ts keys out pixels within distance 64 of #FF00FF
assets.prompt: <subject in full>, centered and filling most of a square 1:1 frame, <style> illustration style, even flat lighting, no photorealism, <palette with hex codes>. Place it on a completely uniform solid magenta background, hex #FF00FF, with absolutely no gradient, no vignette, no drop shadow and no reflection, so the background can be removed cleanly afterwards. Do not include any text, letters, numbers, logos or watermarks.
assets.postProcess: The magenta must be one even colour edge to edge, or the chroma-key leaves a halo.
assets.acceptCheck: Subject fills the frame, background is one uniform magenta, no lettering.

afterGenerating: Eyeball every file: zero text / letters / numbers (testplan S10).
For every asset with transparency:true confirm the background is a single flat magenta.
Run `pnpm build` from the repo root; confirm dist/g/<slug>/art/ contains every file (they precache via the `webp` glob, testplan S3).
`git add games/<slug>/public/art` and commit it as its own task.
In games/<slug>/docs/progress.md: mark the art task done and tick the art parts of testplan M17 and S10.
